Table1 individual A.II.1

genotype.statement: Heterozygous NM_006060.6:c.427C>T/p.Arg143Trp explicitly identified in all four affected family members and Sanger confirmed.

evidence.locator: Table1 column A.II.1; Family A results; Figures1A and S1/S3A
Table1 individual A.II.1

limitations: Source lists NC_000007.14:g.50450243C>T, while packet uses g.50382545C>T; methods align to hg19. Assembly/coordinate labeling is inconsistent and exact genomic equivalence was not independently remapped. Coding/protein identity matches.

segregation.statement: Affected mother and all three affected sons carry R143W; unaffected father and daughter are wild type in Figure1. TNFSF10 candidate also co-segregates in the same family.

evidence.locator: Table1 column A.II.1; Family A results; Figures1A and S1/S3A
Table1 individual A.II.1

phase.statement: Single heterozygous IKZF1 allele; sons inherit it maternally by the family segregation. Compound-heterozygous phase is not applicable.

evidence.locator: Table1 column A.II.1; Family A results; Figures1A and S1/S3A
Table1 individual A.II.1

limitations: Origin of the allele in the mother is not established; do not call de novo. TNFSF10 is a separate locus and its cosegregation does not establish a single causal mechanism.

causal_confidence.statement: R143W has direct functional support for impaired target-DNA binding and pericentromeric localization when expressed alone; familial CVID segregation supports relevance.

evidence.locator: Table1 column A.II.1; Family A results; Figures1A and S1/S3A
Table1 individual A.II.1

limitations: Wildtype coexpression retains binding/localization in these heterologous assays; no demonstrated dominant-negative effect here. This does not quantify endogenous patient-cell function.
TNFSF10/TRAIL Gln27Lys also cosegregates and shows model-system defects; its independent/modifying contribution to CVID remains unproved.
Representative overexpression images/gels and one binding motif do not resolve transcriptional effects, penetrance or causal contributions in patient B cells.

All530mainlines/18pages, four figures, two tables, four supplements and full linked corrigendum read. All four assigned FamilyA individuals and80phenotype annotations individually adjudicated; all13source clinical columns and nine family contexts reviewed.

FamilyA coding/protein allele supported; printed NC_000007.14:g.50450243 coordinate versus packetg.50382545 and hg19 methods is an unresolved assembly-label discrepancy. No exact genomic normalization claimed.

Negative autoantibodies and many specific clinical exclusions are unreported. ALLNo and splenomegalyYes/No are explicit, bounded to assessment. A.II.1CD19106 is normal; other familyAcounts20/29/72low. A.II.2plasmablast4.7is high, not normal; exclusion of decrease remains supported.

Memory-B-cell label compresses IgA/IgG-switched subsets; only IgG-memory is low in A.II.2. Increased transitional fraction in other familyAmembers does not establish increased absolute transitional count; authors say absolute counts normal.

R143Walone impairs DNA-binding/localization, coexpression preserves wildtype activity; no dominant-negative effect shown under tested conditions. Equal plasmid amounts and expected25/50/25dimer fractions are assumptions, not measured stoichiometry. Mobility shift does not independently identify exact dimer/multimer composition.

K286truncatedprotein31kDa enters nucleus and binds tested motif, despite summary causal wording implying DNA-binding defect. Predicted haploinsufficiency from sequence is not proof protein decay. H119R/V139A/M494fsnotfunctionallytested; normal available assays for G337S/A448Rdo not prove benignity. M494V oligomerization effect distinct from DNA-binding/pericentromeric defect; Table2does not call it loss of function.

FamilyA TNFSF10candidate cosegregates but mechanistic/clinical contribution unresolved. S3Bdiagramc79C>A versus main/S3Cc79G>T labeling; B/Ccaptions swapped. No precise alternative HGVS repair invented.

S3Jdoseaxis0.05/0.2/0.8/3.2/12.8 differs from caption1.6–12.8range. S3Eis a single24hco-culture snapshot, not demonstrated kinetic delay; annexin-positive and membrane-integrity quadrants must not be conflated. S3F/Gsupports less cell death in mutant co-culture. Replicate n/statistical methods for significance annotations are not specified.

S3M/Iplots appear identical in separate context sections; no independent-replicate claim. ERlocalization is inferred from diffuse cytoplasm/internal staining without an ER-specific marker. Glycosylation/cleavage interpreted from blot bands, not independent biochemical identification.
